data.title: 'The Peak May Be Here,' Says Top Investor About Nvidia Stock
data.description:
Nvidia (NASDAQ:NVDA) stock briefly looked ready for a comeback after delivering another strong earnings report, but concerns surrounding Jensen Huang's absence ultimately overshadowed the chip giant's financial performance. Its encouraging results and outlook initially sent shares soaring nearly 5.5%, suggesting investors were prepared to look beyond the former CEO's departure. However, that enthusiasm proved short-lived, with the stock reversing course to close Wednesday down 2.9%, extending its losses to about 37% from its early October peak.

At such a steep discount, some investors might be wondering whether Nvidia has finally become too tempting to ignore. However, before pulling the trigger, they may want to hear from investor Victor Dergunov, who ranks among the top 3% of stock experts on TipRanks.

Despite acknowledging the company's outstanding financial performance, Dergunov believes staying on the sidelines remains the safer choice, warning that its strongest growth years may already be behind it.

The investor focuses on three areas that could determine where NVDA shares go next: revenue growth, profitability, and spending by its largest customers. His conclusion offers little encouragement to those expecting a rebound anytime soon.

"The base case scenario is that 2026 will mark the peak in all three," Dergunov opined.

That outlook suggests Nvidia could face a prolonged cooling period, potentially limiting future investment returns despite continued operational success.

For now, however, Nvidia's financial performance remains outstanding. Its latest quarterly results included revenue growth exceeding 100% year-over-year for the second consecutive period. Meanwhile, Nvidia has raised its fiscal 2028 revenue growth outlook to 75%, up from its previous projection of 70%.

Yet, Dergunov sees reasons for caution, pointing toward the company's shrinking price-to-sales multiple despite repeated earnings beats. This trend suggests the market has become less willing to reward Nvidia's achievements with generous valuations.

Profitability presents another concern as the company prepares for higher expenses alongside weaker margins. The company expects GAAP gross margin to range between 71% and 72% next quarter, while operating costs are projected to climb toward $11 billion.

Looking further ahead, Nvidia expects gross margins to recover to between 72% and 73% in fiscal 2028, although that would remain below the 74.8% reported in its latest quarter. Such developments, according to Dergunov, could weigh on earnings potential, regardless of continued strength in customer orders.

Perhaps the biggest concern, however, involves Nvidia's largest clients and their appetite for expensive computing infrastructure. Microsoft, Amazon, Alphabet, Meta, and Oracle have poured billions into expanding data centers, helping drive the semiconductor manufacturer's extraordinary sales figures. Dergunov calculates that their combined capital expenditures have now exceeded operating cash flow, raising doubts about how long this pace can continue. Should these tech companies begin moderating investments, Nvidia could face a tougher environment than its latest quarterly figures suggest.

Ultimately, Dergunov believes investors should distinguish between owning a successful enterprise and purchasing an attractive investment at current prices.

"Strong quarterly results do not mean above-market shareholder returns," the investor wrote.

For now, Dergunov assigns NVDA shares a Hold (i.e., Neutral) rating, suggesting investors may be better served waiting for greater clarity before committing additional capital. (To watch Dergunov's track record, click here)

Wall Street, however, remains more bullish on Nvidia's prospects, with the stock earning a Moderate Buy consensus rating based on 30 Buys, 13 Holds, and just one Sell. Still, analysts were far more enthusiastic just two weeks ago, before a wave of downgrades brought the number of Hold recommendations to 13. Nonetheless, the average 12-month price target of $232.59 suggests an upside potential of 54% from current levels. (See NVDA stock forecast)

data.title: Market Turns to Anthropic's IPO
data.description:
Stock futures are little changed as the market awaits the highly anticipated initial public offering (IPO) of artificial intelligence (AI) company Anthropic (ANT) on Nov. 19. Shares of the company behind the Claude chatbot are expected to begin trading on the Nasdaq Composite exchange under the ticker symbol "ANT."

Anthropic upsized its offering late on Nov. 18, saying in a statement that it is responding to strong demand for its stock among investors. In a press release, Anthropic said that it plans to sell 980 million shares at $83 each. The company had initially planned to sell 825 million shares at a price between $70 and $78. But strong demand led Anthropic to increase its shares on offer and their price.

In the futures market, the blue-chip Dow Jones Industrial Average was rising 0.12%, the benchmark S&P 500 index was up 0.35%, and the technology-heavy Nasdaq was gaining 0.80%.

Anthropic's Big Day

With its upwardly revised offering, Anthropic is on track to raise $81.3 billion from its IPO, surpassing SpaceX (SPCX), which held a record IPO in June that raised $75 billion. The final valuation of Anthropic is expected to be slightly above the $1.4 trillion that it was targeting in the share sale.

Investors and analysts now wait to see how ANT stock performs in its market debut. Market commentators quoted in The Wall Street Journal and Barron's say the IPO is a test for the AI industry, which has experienced volatility in recent weeks as concerns grow about the sustainability of the money being spent on data centers and other infrastructure.

Big Losses at Anthropic

In particular, there are concerns that rising interest rates will make debt unaffordable for many data center developers and AI companies. Stocks of AI companies have also been volatile since Jensen Huang resigned as CEO of Nvidia (NVDA). Huang was seen as a champion and leader for the entire AI ecosystem.

While Anthropic is growing at a rapid rate, the company remains unprofitable. In its IPO prospectus, Anthropic said that it generated $33.24 billion in revenue, up 1,200% from the same period in 2025. But the company reported a $104 billion net loss during the first nine months of this year. That's up more than fourfold from the same stretch in 2025 when Anthropic reported a loss of $25 billion.

data.title: 3 'Strong Buy' High-Risk Stocks That Could Deliver 100% or More Gains
data.description:
Aurora Innovation (AUR), SanDisk Corp. (SNDK), and Praxis Precision Medicines (PRAX) are three high-risk, high-reward stocks analysts see as having massive upside potential. Wall Street rates each a Strong Buy and projects at least 100% upside. AUR leads the pack with about 193% upside potential.

These companies operate in fast-changing markets. In such markets, investor sentiment can shift quickly as conditions change. That volatility creates significant risk, but also the potential for huge gains. This is especially true if the companies deliver on their growth strategies.

These stocks have a beta greater than two. In other words, their shares are more than twice as volatile as the broader market.

Aurora Innovation (AUR)

Aurora is a U.S. self-driving tech startup known for the Aurora Driver. This advanced platform combines hardware, software, and data services to enable self-driving. Aurora was founded in 2017 in Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania. It is now racing toward the commercial rollout of its technology.

On Wall Street, AUR has a Strong Buy consensus, with six Buys and two Holds issued over the past three months. The average AUR price target of $11.43 suggests about 193% upside ahead.

SanDisk Corp. (SNDK)

This is an American storage company. It develops and makes storage products based on NAND flash memory. This refers to non-volatile memory, meaning it stores data even when power is off. This technology is used in products such as solid-state drives, memory cards, and USB drives.

On Wall Street, SNDK carries a Strong Buy consensus, with 11 Buys and three Holds assigned over the past three months. This comes with an average price target of $2,131, suggesting about 175% upside.

Praxis Precision Medicines (PRAX)

Praxis is an American biopharma company. It makes drugs to treat brain and nerve conditions.

The company is currently seeking regulatory approval for its lead drug candidates. Relutrigine is designed to treat rare, severe seizure disorders. Similarly, ulixacaltamide is designed to treat uncontrollable shaking, especially in the hands.

On Wall Street, PRAX has a Strong Buy consensus rating. This reflects 13 Buys issued by analysts over the past three months. This comes with an average price target of $738.15, implying about 142% upside.

data.title: Leopold Aschenbrenner Plans Hedge Fund Comeback After 67% Loss
data.description:
Leopold Aschenbrenner is considering a return to leveraged investing just four months after his AI-focused hedge fund, Situational Awareness, lost 67% in July and required an emergency rescue from billionaire Ken Griffin's Citadel. The 25-year-old has discussed plans for "Situational Awareness 2.0" with brokers and investors, according to the Financial Times. The fund still manages more than $10 billion, primarily through private investments.

The proposed comeback would reverse a promise Aschenbrenner made after July's losses. At the time, he told investors that his fund would stop borrowing money to increase the size of its investments.

Before the collapse, Situational Awareness had gained 439% during the first six months of 2026. However, the fund relied heavily on borrowed money to achieve those returns. When AI stocks subsequently declined, lenders demanded additional collateral to protect themselves against further losses.

As a result, the fund was forced to sell most of its publicly traded holdings to Citadel to repay its lenders. Despite the 67% July decline, Reuters reported that Situational Awareness was still up by approximately 80% for the year. In addition, Aschenbrenner returned to the market in September with new investments in AI-related companies. His largest reported stock position was a $440.7 million stake in Australian cloud computing company SharonAI (SHAZ).

Now, Aschenbrenner has reportedly held talks with investment bank Jefferies (JEF) about opening a prime brokerage account. The bank previously rejected the fund over its inadequate hedging. Meanwhile, banking giant JPMorgan Chase (JPM) terminated its lending relationship with Situational Awareness in September.

Anthropic IPO Could Help the Fund's Comeback

Although Situational Awareness suffered heavy losses in public markets, its private investments could provide financial support for a restart. The fund reportedly owns an approximately $5 billion stake in AI developer Anthropic (ANT), which is expected to begin trading on the Nasdaq on November 19.

Anthropic's IPO could value the company at approximately $1.4 trillion, compared with the $965 billion valuation it received during its May funding round. That increase would make Situational Awareness's remaining stake considerably more valuable.

Anthropic's financial results also explain the interest. Revenue surged to $33.24 billion during the first nine months of 2026, compared with less than $2.55 billion a year earlier. Meanwhile, its operating loss narrowed to $1.26 billion from $5.22 billion.

Separately, Situational Awareness has discussed raising additional capital from outside investors in early 2027. However, those plans have not been finalized.

data.title: Anthropic Prices IPO at $83, Setting Up $94 Billion Stock Sale
data.description:
AI developer Anthropic (ANT) has reportedly priced its initial public offering (IPO) at $83 per share, which is 6.4% above the top of its original $70 to $78 range. According to Bloomberg, the company also increased the size of the offering. Based on the previously disclosed share count, the IPO would raise at least $68.5 billion. When combined with a separate $26 billion private placement, the total would exceed $94 billion.

At that size, Anthropic's combined fundraising would surpass the $86.2 billion raised by space exploration company SpaceX (SPCX) during its June IPO, which includes additional shares sold through an option granted to underwriters.

The higher price also gives Anthropic an estimated fully diluted valuation of approximately $1.5 trillion ahead of its expected Nasdaq (NDAQ) debut on Thursday, November 19.

Before the reported increase in offering size, Anthropic planned to sell 801.4 million shares, while existing shareholders were offering another 23.6 million. The company will not receive proceeds from shares sold by those shareholders.

data.title: Why Did RIOT Stock Climb Today, November 18?
data.description:
Shares of AI data center developer Riot Platforms (RIOT) jumped by 6.98% to $18.24 on Wednesday. This followed bullish views from activist investor Starboard Value. According to Bloomberg, Starboard CEO Jeff Smith sees Riot as one of two companies the market has undervalued. As a result, the stock could benefit from growing demand for data center infrastructure.

Starboard Is Bullish on Riot Platforms

Riot started as a biotech company. It now operates as a Bitcoin mining and digital infrastructure business.

Notably, Smith's note comes as Riot's shares have fallen about 26% year-to-date. This comes amid a recent selloff in Bitcoin and digital assets.

The company also reported a net loss of $733.6 million across the first nine months of 2026. What's more, AI infrastructure stocks recently sold off due to worries about high borrowing costs.

However, Smith believes the company can deliver revenue growth. This information is based on an investor presentation seen by the news outlet. Smith is scheduled to speak at the Capitalized for Kids Investor Conference in Toronto.

The other company the Starboard CEO sees as undervalued is industrial equipment maker Flowserve (FLS).

How Is Riot Platforms Doing?

In the third quarter, Riot saw its revenue rise roughly 1% year-over-year to $181.43 million. This beat the consensus of $160.82 million.

However, the company's earnings per share plunged 96% to $0.01. This beat Wall Street's estimate of a $0.34 loss per share.

Interestingly, during its recent earnings, the company said its contracted data-center portfolio now stood at 1,151 megawatts. This followed three leases with Advanced Micro Devices (AMD) and a top AI lab.

On financing, Gautam Chhugani, a five-star analyst at Bernstein (AB), recently maintained his Buy rating on the stock. He noted that Riot has about $1.2 billion in liquidity to keep new data-center construction on track.

Is Riot Platforms a Good Stock to Buy?

On Wall Street, analysts have a Strong Buy consensus rating on Riot Platforms' shares. This reflects 14 Buys and one Hold issued over the past three months.

In addition, the average RIOT price target of $34.29 implies about 88% upside (see RIOT stock forecast here).

data.title: U.S. Stocks End Mostly Lower as Nvidia Rally Fades and Expectations Rise for Interest Rate Hikes
data.description:
U.S. equity markets ended broadly lower following a volatile trading session on Nov. 18. Data from CNBC showed that the blue-chip Dow Jones Industrial Average shed 561 points, or 1.11% on the day, while the benchmark S&P 500 traded down 0.23%. The technology-laden Nasdaq Composite index see-sawed between gains and losses throughout the trading session before eking out a 0.42% advance.

Stocks were choppy as the post-earnings bounce in Nvidia (NVDA) faded. Shares of the chipmaker had been up 4% immediately after it reported blockbuster third-quarter financial results. However, NVDA stock sank during the day and ended up closing down 2% as investors continue to take a wait-and-see approach to the company after CEO Jensen Huang resigned last week.

Interest Rate Expectations

Also exerting downward pressure on stocks was the release of the minutes from the U.S. Federal Reserve's October policy meeting. The minutes show consensus building among central bank officials for further interest rate hikes in coming months.

"Almost all participants judged that, under their baseline outlooks for inflation and the labor market, further action to raise the target range for the federal funds rate would likely be appropriate, in order to ensure a timely return of inflation to the 2 percent objective," read the meeting minutes.

Financial markets are pricing in a 98% chance that the Fed raises interest rates another 25 basis points at the conclusion of its next policy meeting on Dec. 9, according to data from LSEG (LSEG). Higher interest rates, which raise the cost of borrowing for companies, are seen as a negative for stocks and drag on corporate earnings.

Stock Winners and Losers

Stocks that outperformed the market on Nov. 18 included:

  • Okta (OKTA)
  • Generac (GNRC)
  • TJX Companies (TJX)
  • Walt Disney (DIS)
  • Amazon (AMZN)

Equities that underperformed on the day included:

  • UnitedHealth (UNH)
  • Humana (HUM)
  • Strategy (MSTR)
  • CoreWeave (CRWV)
  • Salesforce (CRM)

data.title: Another Shakeup Hits Skydance TV; Skydance Stock (NYSE:SKYD) Slides
data.description:
Entertainment giant Skydance (SKYD) recently announced another change in the making for its television operations, one of the biggest and possibly most controversial parts of its corporate structure. The two studios—Warner Bros. Television Group and Paramount Television Studios—will be unifying under one management body. Skydance stock slid nearly 3% in the closing minutes of Wednesday's trading. Skydance has seen a 56.99% loss in its share price over the past year.

Bringing the Operations Together

Interestingly, Skydance plans to keep the Warner Bros. branding when it makes this combination. Warner Bros. Television Group and Paramount Television Studios will ultimately become Warner Bros. Television Studios. The new organization will officially launch early next year, but will continue to operate independently for the remaining six weeks of this year.

Once completed, the resulting combination will have over 120 active television series to its credit, ranging from Reacher to Landman and beyond. In charge of the combined operation will be Matt Thunell and Channing Dungey, who both had plenty of praise for each other. Dungey described Thunell as having "…extraordinary creative instincts," and Thunell noting that Dungey was "…one of the most accomplished and respected executives in our industry…."

And About That Tax Credit…

Meanwhile, Skydance's David Ellison recently hit the Dealbook summit, according to a Deadline report, to talk about a potential upcoming tax credit designed to support film and television efforts. Most can likely think of a better use for tax dollars than this—including giving said dollars back to the taxpayer so they can buy groceries and the like—but Ellison noted that the tax credit was not going to line celebrity actors' pockets, but rather, those of normal, below-the-line workers.

Ellison noted, "Tom Cruise, the biggest talent in the world, are going to get paid whatever they get paid, no matter where they shoot in the world. It is the union workers, it is the makeup artists, it is the craftsmen, it is the set builders that fundamentally are being subsidized. You are creating jobs." Given how many of those jobs have been lost throughout Hollywood in recent years, any help in getting them back will likely be welcome.

data.title: New Study Puts AI Bubble Chances at 97% – Here's Why
data.description:
A new study has found that artificial intelligence stocks had a 97% probability of being in a bubble as of September 2026, according to its strongest model. However, two other versions put the probability closer to 40%. The findings come from researchers who analyzed nearly 800,000 financial news articles going back 170 years. Importantly, the 97% figure measures how closely today's market resembles past bubbles rather than the likelihood of an imminent stock market crash.

According to the Financial Times, researchers Marco Grotteria, Afonso Monteiro, and Constantine Yannelis examined 795,964 articles from The Economist published between 1843 and 2013. They found that financial news articles historically suggested there was a 20% chance of a major market crash within the next six months. However, historical data showed that crashes actually happened only 5.7% of the time.

This means that the warnings overstated the actual risk by roughly three and a half times.

However, the researchers also found that changes in the intensity of those warnings contained useful information. Their model compared news coverage with 22 historical market bubbles and tracked signs of excessive speculation and concerns about expensive stock valuations.

When tested, the model correctly ranked a randomly selected bubble month above a normal month 74% of the time. That figure increased to 94% for the dot-com bubble.

Why the Latest AI Bubble Warning Stands Out

The latest reading is particularly high compared to previous market crises. The same model recorded a 92% probability near the peak of the dot-com bubble in 2000 and 97% during the 2007 financial crisis.

There are also financial reasons why AI valuations are receiving attention. The Federal Reserve recently reported that debt issuance related to advanced computing had reached $680 billion by October 2026, roughly five times the amount issued during all of 2023.

That matters because companies must continue making debt payments even if their AI investments generate less revenue than expected. Meanwhile, a recent Federal Reserve survey found that 87% of respondents considered AI a financial stability risk, up from 50% in May.

However, the researchers pointed out some limitations in their study. For example, their historical analysis relied on one publication, while the AI models used to examine old articles might have recognized events from their training data. They also pointed out that technologies such as the internet created genuine economic value despite experiencing major investment bubbles.

data.title: Micron Still Sees Memory Supply Shortage Through 2028 — MU Stock Falls
data.description:
Shares of U.S. memory chipmaker Micron (MU) dropped 2% to about $699 during Wednesday's afternoon trading. This came even as CEO Sanjay Mehrotra maintained the company's earlier outlook on the memory chip supply shortage. He still expects demand to outpace supply through 2028.

Mehrotra spoke Wednesday at the TomorrowX Summit tech conference in Austin, Texas. He noted that demand for the company's products remains "robust" and supply "continues to be tight."

His comments come as Micron recently reported fourth fiscal quarter revenue of $54.23 billion, up 379% from the same period last year. Its adjusted earnings per share also grew 11 times over to $33.42.

Micron Says 2027 Capacity Is Sold Out

At the event, Mehrotra also noted that industry pricing remains positive for the company.

"You know, we have said before that calendar year 2027 and 2028 will be even tighter than 2026," the Micron CEO said.

He continued, "Seventy-five percent of our 2027 [capacity] is sold out. We are in discussions with customers now moving to 2028… We delivered a record 2026, and 2027 is going to be even stronger."

Why RBC Capital Remains Bullish on Micron Stock

Over the past three months, Micron shares have fallen by about 24%. This comes amid Nvidia's leadership crisis (NVDA). This matters because Micron's NAND and DRAM memory chips are usually paired with Nvidia's GPUs in data centers.

The stock also dropped after Democrats regained control of Congress at the U.S. midterm election earlier this month. Investors were worried about stricter data center regulation under Democratic political leadership.

However, five-star RBC Capital analyst Srini Pajjuri sees the recent pullback as "an excellent opportunity." The analyst said he attended an investor meeting with the company's executives.

He pointed out that "management continues to expect [the] industry supply environment to be tighter in 2027/2028 vs. 2026 due to strong AI demand." Pajjuri maintained his Buy rating on Micron. He also kept his price target at $1,500, predicting about 115% upside.

Is Micron Stock a Good Buy?

On Wall Street, Micron's shares continue to have a Strong Buy consensus rating. This is based on 28 Buys and one Hold assigned over the past three months.

In addition, the average MU price target of $1,624 implies about 133% upside (see MU stock forecast here).
